title: Approve remote Cyclotron CLI login through a scoped single-use transaction
description:
Requested by Ryan for Claude through Kanbus (2026-10-30). This filing authorizes issue records only; implementation and any live identity/backend changes are subsequent work. No production login, deployment, IAM changes, secrets in chat, or direct message to Claude. Dot must operate from cloud/headless Linux without a Mac or AWS CLI. Optional shared auth libraries must not combine the two CLI products. Write executable behavioral specifications before implementation; use fake providers/stores in automated tests, and separately record any approved live evidence.

As a lab user, I want to approve a waiting cloud CLI using a URL on another device, with no secret or auth-code handoff through chat.

Acceptance: explicit login waits with bounded polling and can be cancelled/denied/expire. Evaluate a secure broker or equivalent provider-supported handoff; Cognito User Pools must not be presumed to provide RFC 8628. Document trust boundaries, required backend endpoints and availability, issuer/audience validation, anti-CSRF/state, CLI possession proof, single-use redemption, short expiry, replay prevention, rate limits/backoff and cleanup. Approval displays requester and exact lab/account/scope, requires authenticated authorization, and cannot broaden grants. Redemption is bound to the originating CLI; a copied URL cannot redeem the session. Persist renewable material only through the secure lifecycle story; no secrets in logs, argv, environment, repositories or chat. Noninteractive commands never open a browser unexpectedly.

Feature: Cross-device lab login
  Scenario: Authorized approval
    Given a cloud CLI requests a scoped lab/account login
    When the authorized user opens its HTTPS URL on another device and approves
    Then only that CLI receives the matching renewable session
  Scenario: Malicious or stale handoff
    Given a replayed, expired, denied or target-substituted transaction
    When redemption is attempted
    Then it yields no session

References: src/decision_flywheel/account_routes.py; account_sessions.py and their tests; docs/decision-contract.md. Related existing signed-challenge story decision-flywheel-69e1e477-f42b-470f-a438-047de108e1e8; counterpart Papyrus PPY-5a3624d4-4f1a-4eee-9bb6-12e575ec3cad. Reuse reviewed security concepts without requiring the Papyrus CLI or assuming browser cookies are renewable native credentials.

comments.author: home
comments.text: Plan (Claude, 2026-10-30), see docs/cli-remote-login.md: the same split-secret broker as Papyrus PPY-5a3624. The CLI keeps PKCE verifier V and poll secret P, POSTs /start (client, lab, S256(V), sha256(P), requester label), gets T, a matching code, https://lab.cyclotron.anth.us/cli/approve?t=T, a poll interval and ~10 min expiry. Approve redirects to Cognito with the transaction's challenge and redirect /cli/callback, state = T + cookie-bound nonce; the callback stores the code on T; /poll with T + P returns it once (conditional delete); the CLI exchanges it with V. The broker never holds a token. Live prerequisites, both needing Ryan's approval: the callback https://lab.cyclotron.anth.us/cli/callback on cyclotron-console-public (defined in the Prospectus repo), and the broker Lambda, function URL and DynamoDB table in the lab stack. A person must have signed in to the lab in a browser once (Prospectus enrollment).

comments.author: home
comments.text: Decided (Ryan, 2026-10-30): keep the throttling on both brokers (per-caller rate limits on /start and /poll, slow_down), and keep the best choices from both plans. The Papyrus plan now also takes this plan's additions (AnthusAI/Papyrus#882). See docs/cli-remote-login.md.

comments.author: home
comments.text: Live on the lab since 2026-10-30. cyclotron login --remote prints an approval URL and code; Ryan approved from his phone, the CLI enrolled the login at Prospectus (cli-login 0.3.0 hooks, POST /cli/enroll), and cyclotron whoami answered his person and three accounts. The broker (stack cyclotron-cli-broker) runs cli-login 0.3.0; it had been left on 0.2.0, which dropped the enrollment nonce until it was updated on 2026-10-30. Shipped in Decision-Flywheel #179 and #181; deploy record #180.
